note.text: A balance sheet records a position at a date. From the bank’s perspective, reserves, loans granted and securities held are assets. Customer deposits are liabilities because the bank owes them. Equity is assets less liabilities, so assets equal liabilities plus equity. A customer may view their deposit as an asset without making it an asset of the bank. Balancing the equation does not prove that every asset will be repaid or available for an immediate payment. The model omits other real reporting categories.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to classify bank assets and liabilities and reconcile them with equity. Builds on: commercial-bank deposits, lending and risk. Leads to: paired credit-creation entries and simplified expansion models.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: Original bank record: reserves {5000}, loans {12000}, securities {3000}; deposits {18000}, equity {2000} CFA francs. Assets total {5000+12000+3000}; deposits plus equity total {18000+2000}. The same customer loan is an asset for the lender and a debt for the borrower. No actual bank statement is used.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Fix the bank’s perspective, classify each line and sum assets. Subtract all stated liabilities for equity, then reconcile both sides. Do not add a loan’s borrower debt as a second liability of the lending bank. Separate a stock balance sheet from income during a period.

cards.idea: Distinguish the monetary concepts before evaluating a case.
example: bank asset: a resource or claim held by the bank.
bank liability: an obligation the bank owes to another party.
equity: the residual of assets after liabilities.
balance-sheet identity: assets equalling liabilities plus equity.

cards.idea: Use the stated case evidence to identify the economic feature.
example: A granted customer loan is a claim on repayment.
Customer deposits are owed by the bank.
Subtract deposits from the stated complete asset total.
Both sides reconcile in the invented record.

cards.idea: Explain a consequence instead of assuming every option has the same effect.
example: bank asset: It is a lender asset and borrower liability.
bank liability: Deposit claims differ from owners’ residual interests.
equity: The residual excludes claims owed to others.
balance-sheet identity: The identity does not eliminate risk.
